meta.title: Hetu Luoshu — A local workspace for story worlds

features.title: Big stories need a clear foundation.
features.intro: Keep multiple books in one library, with distinct writing, source checks, reference drafts and versions. External agents are optional; authors make the decisions.

items.title: One story bible. A connected world.
items.body: Keep characters, factions, places and timelines together. Checks cite sources and make uncertainty visible.
items.alt: Xiaotu holding a story scroll linked to character cards and an author lock

items.title: Structure the adaptation from your novel.
items.body: Organize plot beats and scenes from existing text, with source mappings. You or an external agent provide new dialogue.
items.alt: A novel manuscript, scene cards and a clapperboard

items.title: Adopt excerpts. Finalize separately.
items.body: Review records a decision. Preview selected changes before adopting them into working text, then finalize an exact revision. Earlier finals remain available.
items.alt: Xiaotu organizing reviewed manuscripts and a delivery box

workflow.title: From the first chapter to the next medium.
workflow.intro: Move from a multi-book library to a focused workspace. Reviewing a reference, adopting it and finalizing text are separate decisions. Work manually or choose an external agent.

steps.title: Create a book and its canon
steps.body: Keep each book’s details, cover, chapters and story bible independent. Begin planning without a title or an agent.

steps.title: Write and adapt
steps.body: Write chapters, organize existing plot beats, then outline episodes and scenes. The core structures material; it does not invent dialogue.

steps.title: Review, adopt, finalize
steps.body: Inspect sources and checks, then record a review. Adopt selected text into an editable manuscript and finalize a saved revision separately.

steps.title: Save and version
steps.body: Saving text and creating Git snapshots are separate. Prepare fixed files, identity and changes for author approval. Remote collaboration needs its own authorization.

details.title: Suggestions are not canon
details.body: Discovered names, places and relationships remain candidates. Only author-confirmed content enters the story bible.

details.title: Checks are not literary judges
details.body: Rules inspect explicit facts and structure, reporting coverage and uncertainty. Motivation and literary choices stay with the author.

details.title: Review, adoption and finalization are separate
details.body: Review approval does not overwrite text. Adoption saves a new working revision; finalization records an author decision on an exact revision. Later edits retain earlier finals.

details.title: Prepare delivery from actual capabilities
details.body: Keep Markdown or Fountain sources, provenance and local versions. Check the recipient’s template. Complete bundles and format conversion depend on the specific release capabilities.

open.title: The tools keep it together. The story is yours.
open.body: No built-in models or generation-service lock-in. Readable files, Git history and open MCP let you choose your own creative process.

integrations.eyebrow: Help your assistant understand your story
integrations.title: Agents assist. Authors decide.
integrations.intro: A survival story and an urban slice of life need different writing methods. Choose a suite for this book and use it with your own Codex, Claude Code or WorkBuddy, or write entirely on your own.

layers.title: Say what you want to work on
layers.body: A title, an outline, a passage of dialogue or a cover: ask for one thing at a time and include the story details you have already decided.

layers.title: Choose methods for this book
layers.body: Find one Skills suite that fits your genre. If you are unsure, discuss the direction with your assistant before making the choice yourself.

layers.title: Read the suggestion and decide
layers.body: An assistant offers suggestions. Check the characters and plot, keep the parts you want, and make the final decision about your manuscript.

integrations.status: Writing methods are installed in the external assistant you choose. The homepage is a demo and does not install or connect an assistant.
integrations.manual: A complete workflow without an agent
integrations.manualBody: Create books, write chapters and organize characters and world details yourself. Bring in an assistant when you want help and keep your own pace.

formats.title: Editable for authors. Readable for recipients.
formats.body: Current manuscripts use Markdown and independent scripts use Fountain. DOCX, PDF and complete bundles are delivery designs whose availability depends on the release capabilities. Check recipient templates, Chinese typography and media rights.

faq.title: Know the boundaries before you begin.

items.q: Will Hetu Luoshu write my novel for me?
items.a: No. Write yourself or ask your own Codex, Claude Code or WorkBuddy to discuss ideas and prepare reference drafts. Hetu Luoshu organizes your books, story details and revisions. You decide what to use.

items.q: Can an agent change my story bible?
items.a: An assistant working through a Hetu Luoshu task cannot unlock your story bible or approve final text for you. When using other tools, also check which files you have allowed them to access.

items.q: Will consistency checks detect every out-of-character moment?
items.a: No. Written facts about characters, time and world rules are easier to check; complex motivations and personality still need your judgment. Checks provide clues for your own review.

items.q: Which platforms and languages are included?
items.a: The current focus is Mac, with Simplified Chinese and English interfaces. Windows and mobile clients are not part of this release.

Version 0.3.0 provides source code and the homepage demo, without a ready-to-install app package. Users with a development environment can build the Mac app. Authors can start directly in the homepage demo.

items.q: Will my work be uploaded or become open source?
items.a: Your own books stay in the local folder you choose. Open-source software does not make your novel open source. You choose whether to share material with an external assistant or sync it elsewhere.

items.q: How do I deliver a novel or script?
items.a: Check the editor or recipient's required format, then use the export options available in your client. The homepage demo lets you try the workflow and does not create submission files.

items.q: What are the license and costs?
items.a: The source code uses the Apache-2.0 open-source license. Accounts and service fees for external assistants are handled by those clients. Hetu Luoshu does not sell model services.
